content.summary: Welcome to the reading mission on architectural wonders and historic landmarks. In this lesson, you will read about famous buildings around the world, learn how to describe when and where they were built, and practice reading strategies to find key details quickly.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Past passive voice (was/were built) and location phrases (is located in, stands in).
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Words related to historic buildings, materials, and design features.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Scanning texts to find specific dates, locations, and names of buildings.

learningObjectives: Understand short reading texts about famous buildings and historic landmarks.
Find specific details like dates, locations, and architectural features in a text.
Use past passive structures correctly to talk about when structures were built.

contextWarmup.prompt: When you travel to a new city, what is the first historic landmark you usually want to visit?
options: A tall skyscraper with modern glass design
An ancient castle or stone fortress
A quiet local park with trees
contextWarmup.explanation: Historic landmarks often include ancient castles and stone fortresses that tell stories about the past.

rules: Use 'was built' or 'were built' to state construction years: 'The temple was built in 1200' or 'The pyramids were built over 4,000 years ago.'
Use 'is located in' or 'stands in' to mention the position of a landmark: 'The Eiffel Tower is located in Paris' or 'Big Ben stands in London.'
Use adjective plus noun combinations to describe architectural features: 'massive stone walls', 'golden dome', 'tall skyscraper.'
Use 'It is famous for...' or 'It is known as...' to explain significance: 'It is famous for its unique design' or 'It is known as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.'
Use accurate time prepositions: 'in the 15th century', 'during the Renaissance', 'centuries ago', 'in 1889'.

commonTrap.explanation: Learners often forget to use 'was' or 'were' when describing past construction in reading texts.
commonTrap.correct: Always include 'was' or 'were' before the past participle: 'The temple was built in 1400.'

paragraphs: Every year, millions of travelers visit famous architectural wonders and historic landmarks. One of the most popular attractions in Europe is the Eiffel Tower, which is located in Paris. This tall iron structure was built in 1889 by a famous architect named Gustave Eiffel. Today, it stands as a symbol of French culture and welcomes visitors from all over the world.

Another incredible historic landmark is the Colosseum in Rome, Italy. This ancient stone fortress and amphitheater was built almost two thousand years ago. It is famous for its massive stone walls and beautiful arches. Visitors love walking around the ruins and learning about its fascinating history as a cultural heritage site.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Architectural Wonders & Historic Landmarks

content.summary: Learn how to write clear descriptions of famous buildings, ancient temples, and historic landmarks using correct passive structures, location phrases, and descriptive adjectives.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Stating Location & Foundation
blueprintItems.formula: Landmark + is located in / stands in + City or Country
blueprintItems.example: The Eiffel Tower stands in Paris, France.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Describing Construction & History
blueprintItems.formula: Landmark + was built / were built + in [Year] / by [People]
blueprintItems.example: The ancient temple was built in the 12th century.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Explaining Features & Importance
blueprintItems.example: The castle is famous for its massive stone walls.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always capitalize proper names of landmarks, cities, and countries.
mechanicsRules.badExample: the eiffel tower is in paris.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: The Eiffel Tower is in Paris.
mechanicsRules.why: Names of specific monuments and cities are proper nouns in English.

mechanicsRules.rule: Use 'was' for singular landmarks and 'were' for plural landmarks when writing about past construction.
mechanicsRules.badExample: The pyramids was built thousands of years ago.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: The pyramids were built thousands of years ago.
mechanicsRules.why: Pyramids is plural, so it requires the plural past verb 'were'.

mechanicsRules.rule: Place descriptive adjectives before the noun they modify.
mechanicsRules.badExample: It has a walls stone massive.
mechanicsRules.why: In English, descriptive adjectives come before nouns.

content.summary: Speak clearly about famous buildings and historic places by mastering word stress, sentence rhythm, and intonation at the A2 level.
content.audioGuidance: Pay attention to how we stress important content words like nouns and adjectives when describing architectural wonders.

pillars.name: Vowel Clarity
pillars.target: Clear short and long vowels in descriptive words
pillars.explanation: Pronounce vowels distinctly in words like ancient, dome, and structure so listeners understand your descriptions.

pillars.name: Word Stress
pillars.target: Correct syllable emphasis in multi-syllable terms
pillars.explanation: Place primary stress on the correct syllable in words like architect, monument, and magnificent.

pillars.name: Sentence Rhythm
pillars.target: Linking words naturally in descriptive sentences
pillars.explanation: Connect consonants to vowels smoothly when talking about tourist attractions and historic landmarks.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Notice how the stress shifts to the second syllable in architect.
Single-syllable words carry full stress, while two-syllable nouns stress the first syllable.
Notice how attraction moves the main stress to the second syllable.
Longer adjectives like magnificent place primary stress on the third syllable from the end.
